patch.value: Search pm items in any public GitHub repo (gh-authenticated, semantic search)

pm-github gains the ability to discover and search pm workspaces in ANY public GitHub repository, so an agent can do deep online research: compare how other projects track work, learn conventions from mature pm workspaces, and find prior art for a problem before solving it locally. Uses the gh CLI when the user is authenticated so requests draw on the user's own rate limits rather than an anonymous quota. Must support the pm built-in semantic search over the fetched items, not just literal matching.

Given a public repo (owner/name) pm-github locates its pm workspace (.agents/pm or configured root) via the GitHub API; can list and read items without cloning; supports searching across one or many repos; semantic search works over fetched items using the pm CLI's built-in semantic search; uses gh CLI auth when available and degrades to unauthenticated with a clear rate-limit message; results are token-budgeted and cite repo+path+item id; no writes to remote repos; unit tests plus a real-data test against at least one real public repo

value.author: claude
value.text:
SCOPE DECISION (owner, 2026-07-24): public pm item search does NOT belong in pm-github. It becomes its own hosted service at pm-search.unbrained.dev, and unlike the rest of the fleet its code stays PRIVATE — it is a hosted service, not a public pm package.

Why the separation is right, recorded so this is not re-litigated: a CLI extension can only search repos the caller names, and it must re-fetch and re-index them on every invocation. A hosted service maintains a continuously updated index across every public pm workspace it can discover, so a query answers in milliseconds against the whole corpus instead of seconds against a handful of repos the agent already knew to ask about. Discovery — 'which projects track this problem at all' — is the actual research need, and only a crawled index can answer it.

A prototype of the extension-side approach was built and functionally verified against real repositories before this decision (workspace auto-detection via the history/ ledger, single-request tarball materialization, delegation to the pm CLI's own keyword/semantic/hybrid retrieval, commit-pinned citations). It worked — 1,934 items from unbraind/pm-cli fetched and searched in ~9s cold, ~5s warm — but that measurement is itself the argument for the hosted design: seconds per repo per query does not scale to corpus-wide research. The prototype was reverted from pm-github; the design lessons carry over to the service.

Two upstream issues were filed from building it, and both stand on their own merits regardless of where search lives: pm-cli#685 (extension context exposes only an absolute pm_root, so extension output leaks host paths that core commands never emit) and pm-cli#686 (extension flags cannot be repeatable — an unknown 'repeatable' property is silently ignored and the flag becomes last-wins, which made a 3-repo search silently search 1 and report success).

This item is closed as superseded, not abandoned. Successor: the pm-search service tracked in the companion hub.

patch.value: Superseded by the pm-search hosted service (pm-search.unbrained.dev): corpus-wide search needs a continuously maintained index, not per-invocation fetching inside a CLI extension. Prototype built, verified against real repos, and reverted from pm-github.
